results.reason: The response says the Varga acquisition is a Change of Control requiring Crestline's prior written consent under DA Section 15.4. It says the Disclosure Schedule wrongly says 'notice only; no consent required'. It explains the termination right, the termination fee and the inaccurate consents representation.

The response says Section 14.2, read with the Qualified Transferee definition, allows assignment without Halvorsen's consent to any lab or diagnostic distributor in the Territory. It notes this includes a competitor or a competitor's affiliate because the definition has no exclusion.

The response says First Amendment Section 3.1 restates Section 12.3 so only Section 9 breaches are carved out, dropping the Section 10 and Section 11 carve-outs. It says the amendment controls under Section 17.5, so Halvorsen's claims against Crestline are now capped.
The response states that the original Section 12.3 excluded breaches of Sections 9 and 10 and the indemnification obligations under Section 11.
The response states the cap is 'the amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim'.
The response is a memo with issues listed separately. Each issue has Document/Section, Why it matters for Halvorsen, and Recommended fix headings.
The response concludes that Crestline's consent is required, not merely notice.
The response expressly says the original carve-outs do not apply unless a further amendment is signed.
